"### Chart Description: Liquidity in Domestic and Foreign Currency

This chart tracks the liquidity of the banking sector in Argentina from August 2018 to February 2024, measured as a percentage of total deposits.

#### Chart Components
*   **Vertical Axis (Y-axis):** Percent of deposits, ranging from 0 to 140 in increments of 20.
*   **Horizontal Axis (X-axis):** Time, labeled at approximately six-month intervals from Aug-18 to Feb-24.
*   **Data Series:**
    *   **BCRA papers (Light Blue Bars):** Represents liquidity held in central bank securities.
    *   **Current account in BCRA (Dark Blue Bars):** Represents liquidity held in current accounts at the central bank. Together with BCRA papers, these form a stacked bar chart representing domestic currency liquidity.
    *   **USD reserves (Dark Blue Dashed Line):** Represents liquidity in foreign currency.

#### Estimated Data Values
The following table provides estimated values based on the chart's grid lines at the specific intervals labeled on the x-axis.

| Date | Current account in BCRA (Dark Blue Bar) | BCRA papers (Light Blue Bar) | Total Liquidity (Top of Bar) | USD reserves (Dashed Line) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Aug-18** | ~20% | ~25% | ~45% | ~53% |
| **Feb-19** | ~22% | ~35% | ~57% | ~56% |
| **Aug-19** | ~18% | ~40% | ~58% | ~57% |
| **Feb-20** | ~18% | ~43% | ~61% | ~70% |
| **Aug-20** | ~15% | ~46% | ~61% | ~84% |
| **Feb-21** | ~12% | ~48% | ~60% | ~86% |
| **Aug-21** | ~11% | ~54% | ~65% | ~83% |
| **Feb-22** | ~12% | ~51% | ~63% | ~89% |
| **Aug-22** | ~9% | ~57% | ~66% | ~91% |
| **Feb-23** | ~8% | ~65% | ~73% | ~89% |
| **Aug-23** | ~7% | ~73% | ~80% | ~80% |
| **Feb-24** | ~7% | ~75% | ~82% | ~82% |

#### Key Observations
*   **Total Liquidity Growth:** Combined liquidity (the stacked bars) shows a steady upward trend, increasing from approximately 45% of deposits in August 2018 to over 80% by early 2024.
*   **Shift in Composition:** There is a significant shift in domestic liquidity. The "Current account in BCRA" (dark blue) has generally declined as a share, while "BCRA papers" (light blue) have grown substantially, becoming the dominant component of liquidity.
*   **USD Reserves Volatility:** USD reserves as a percentage of deposits increased steadily from 2018 to a peak of approximately 91% in late 2022, before experiencing volatility and a slight decline toward the end of the period shown."
